scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You lock money in a fixed deposit and the bank pays you extra for doing nothing. Where does that interest come from?

scenes.name: lend
scenes.text: Your deposit doesn't sit in a vault. The bank lends it out as home loans, car loans and business loans.

scenes.name: spread
scenes.text: Borrowers pay the bank a higher rate, and the bank pays you a lower one. The difference is the bank's profit.

scenes.name: lockin
scenes.text: Because you promise not to withdraw for a fixed time, the bank can plan, so it usually pays more than a savings account.

scenes.name: compound
scenes.text: Interest is often added every quarter, and then that interest earns interest too. That's compounding.

scenes.name: break
scenes.text: If you break it early, banks usually cut the rate a little as a penalty.

scenes.name: tax
scenes.text: The interest is taxable income, and in India deposits are insured up to five lakh rupees per bank.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Lend, earn, compound. Your money working quietly. Follow for more on how things really work.
